facts.statement: The Strait of Hormuz reopened Apr 17 following a temporary ceasefire agreed Apr 8, ending what the IEA characterized as the largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market affecting 20% of global supplies. WTI collapsed from a peak near $128/bbl (Apr 2) to $83.85 (Apr 17), a decline of approximately 34%.
facts.source_title: CNBC — Oil prices drop on Hormuz reopening
connections: 61 oil and gas projects ($100.2B) in the pipeline with direct exposure to oil price movements
367 mining projects ($159.5B) with commodity price exposure
WCS differential widened to $16.25/bbl below WTI on Apr 13

facts.statement: Statistics Canada's Labour Force Survey recorded +14,000 jobs in March, a partial recovery after February's 84,000-job loss. Unemployment held at 6.7%. Average hourly wages accelerated to 4.7% YoY ($37.73/hr), the fastest pace since October 2024.
facts.source_title: Statistics Canada — Labour Force Survey, March 2026
connections: Health care +94,000 YoY (+3.3%), largest annual gain among industries; 259 healthcare projects in pipeline
Natural resources +10,000 (+3.0%) in March; 364 mining projects and 63 oil and gas projects tracked

facts.statement: Canada's merchandise trade deficit widened to $5.7B in February from $4.2B (revised January), the largest since August 2025. Exports rose 6.4% to $66.3B while imports surged 8.4% to a record $72.1B.
facts.source_title: Statistics Canada — International merchandise trade, February 2026
connections: 49 manufacturing projects ($67.4B) exposed to trade flows
600 transport/logistics projects with cross-border supply chain linkages

facts.statement: Housing starts fell 6.0% M/M to 235,852 SAAR in March, below the 255,000 consensus. CREA downgraded its forecast citing the oil shock, though it maintained a +1.5% annual price gain projection to $688,955. The MLS HPI declined for a 16th consecutive month (-0.4% M/M). National average home price stood at $673,084 (-0.8% YoY).
connections: BoC rate held at 2.25%; next decision Apr 29 with MPR

facts.statement: Manufacturing sales rebounded 3.6% to $71.2B in February, led by transportation equipment (+18.8%) and primary metals (+4.9% to record $6.5B). Unfilled manufacturing orders reached a record $117.6B. Building permits dropped 8.4% to $12.1B, with non-residential leading the decline (-$1.3B).
connections: 1,671 infrastructure projects ($179.0B) linked to building permit trends

facts.statement: Bloomberg-Nanos Consumer Confidence Index fell to 46.93 (week ended Apr 3), an 11-month low. The expectations sub-index lost nearly 10 points over four weeks. The decline was linked to the Iran war, elevated energy prices, and inflation concerns.
connections: CPI at +1.8% YoY but energy-driven price pressures building
Gasoline price increases linked to Strait of Hormuz disruptions

indicatorContextLines.bocRate: The Bank of Canada overnight rate stands at 2.25%, the seventh consecutive hold. The Summary of Deliberations published Apr 1 noted near-term growth weaker than the January projection and a soft labour market. The next decision is Apr 29, accompanied by the Monetary Policy Report. Market pricing: 96.5% probability of hold.
indicatorContextLines.cpi: Headline CPI rose 1.8% year-over-year in February 2026, within the Bank of Canada 1-3% target band. Provincial CPI ranges from PE +5.4% to ON -1.1%, a 6.5 percentage-point spread. Core CPI median ran at 2.3%, shelter CPI at +1.5%, food CPI at 5.3%, and energy CPI at -14.2%. The March CPI release is scheduled for Apr 20 and is expected to capture initial oil price surge effects.
indicatorContextLines.unemployment: National unemployment held at 6.7% in March 2026 with +14,000 jobs added, a partial recovery after February's 84,000-job loss. The employment rate was unchanged at 60.6% and the participation rate at 64.9%. Average hourly wages rose 4.7% YoY to $37.73/hr, the fastest pace since October 2024. Health care recorded the largest year-over-year gain at +94,000 (+3.3%). Natural resources added 10,000 (+3.0%) in March.
indicatorContextLines.realGdp: Real GDP contracted 0.2% Q/Q (-0.6% annualized) in Q4 2025, down from +0.6% in Q3. Monthly real GDP fell 0.6% M/M in the latest StatCan print. Manufacturing GDP declined 4.6% YoY; management of companies (NAICS 55) fell 21.9% YoY, the deepest annual contraction among 20 industries. Construction rose 1.1% M/M and 2.8% YoY.
indicatorContextLines.housingStarts: Housing starts fell 6.0% M/M to 235,852 SAAR in March, below the 255,000 consensus. The 6-month trend decreased 2.9% to 248,378. YTD actual starts were +9% YoY (49,206 units through March). CREA downgraded its forecast citing the oil shock. MLS HPI fell 0.4% M/M, the 16th consecutive monthly decline. National average home price $673,084 (-0.8% YoY).
indicatorContextLines.tradeBalance: The merchandise trade deficit widened to $5.7B in February from $4.2B (revised January), the largest since August 2025. Exports rose 6.4% to $66.3B (highest since March 2025) while imports surged 8.4% to a record $72.1B.
indicatorContextLines.consumerConfidence: Bloomberg-Nanos Consumer Confidence Index fell to 46.93 (week ended Apr 3), an 11-month low. The expectations sub-index lost nearly 10 points over four weeks. The decline was linked to the Iran war entering its sixth week, elevated energy prices, and inflation concerns.

cross_references.interpretation: Manufacturing GDP contraction of 4.6% YoY intersects with 49 manufacturing projects ($67.4B) in the pipeline. Manufacturing sales rebounded 3.6% to $71.2B in February with unfilled orders at a record $117.6B.
WTI collapse from ~$128 to $83.85 on Strait reopening directly affects 63 oil and gas projects ($100.2B). The WCS differential widened to $16.25/bbl below WTI.
Housing starts declining 6.0% M/M to 235,852 SAAR alongside 16th consecutive MLS HPI monthly decline affects 211 residential projects ($44.4B).
Trade deficit widening to $5.7B, largest since Aug 2025, with imports at record $72.1B. Affects 600 transport/logistics projects and 49 manufacturing projects through cross-border supply chains.
Construction GDP rising 2.8% YoY and employment at 1,998,800 supports 1,671 infrastructure projects ($179.0B). Building permits dropped 8.4% to $12.1B, a forward-looking headwind.

key_developments: Federal Reserve held federal funds target range at 3.50-3.75% on March 18; FOMC signaling one cut in 2026 and one in 2027
S&P 500 recovered from -4% YTD (Apr 1) to 7,022.95 (Apr 13), within 2.32% of Jan 27 all-time high; S&P 500 and Nasdaq posted fresh record closes Apr 14
US Supreme Court struck down several IEEPA emergency tariffs; administration announced temporary 10% global tariff largely exempting CUSMA-compliant goods
Section 232 tariffs restructured Apr 6 with 50% rate on many core metal imports (aluminum, steel, copper); Canada announced 6-month tariff pause on US-origin manufacturing inputs Apr 15
global_package.canada_impact: US rate differential at 125-150 basis points above BoC's 2.25% shapes CAD/USD levels. Section 232 metal tariffs directly affect Canadian steel, aluminum, and copper exporters. Canadian trade deficit widened to $5.7B in February, with the US market remaining the primary export destination for 49 manufacturing and 600 transport-logistics projects tracked in the pipeline.
